Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the RetailX Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to RetailX's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Thompson, CEO; Maria Lopez, CFO; David Chen, COO; Emily Rivera, CMO; and Raj Patel, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, CEO of RetailX.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust gross merchandise value growth and accelerating international expansion. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV reaching $28.7 billion, up 22% year-over-year.

Our focus remains on enhancing our seller ecosystem and scaling high-velocity markets. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our AI-powered personalization tools, which we believe will significantly boost conversion rates and repeat purchases.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience and localized logistics.

We are focused on improving customer acquisition efficiency and lifetime value.

Finally, we are committed to delivering profitable growth through disciplined expense management.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Lopez, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Maria Lopez:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $6.8 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 43.2%, driven by supply chain efficiencies, higher take rates on marketplace transactions, and a favorable shift toward premium categories. Operating expenses were $4.9 billion, representing 72% of revenue. Marketing spend rose modestly to support customer growth but delivered strong returns, with payback periods compressing meaningfully.

Our net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.12 per diluted share. We ended the quarter with $2.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance to GMV of $105-108 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.65 to $4.85.

To provide more context, let's start with our gross merchandise value performance, which is the north star for our marketplace. In Q3, we delivered $28.7 billion in GMV, up 22% year-over-year and 9% quarter-over-quarter. This beat our guidance of 15-18% YoY and 6-8% QoQ, thanks to stronger order volumes, elevated average order values from premium categories, and faster adoption of our AI personalization engine. This growth outpaced the industry average of 12-14%, per eMarketer.

Breaking it down, fashion and beauty surged 28% YoY, powered by our GenAI stylist tool across 1.2 million SKUs, lifting conversions 15%. Electronics grew 19%, aided by exclusive deals with Samsung and Apple. Third-party GMV, now 68% of total, expanded 25% as we added 45,000 net new active sellers, with our Fulfillment by RetailX program cutting their logistics costs 22% via automation in 35 North American hubs.

Regionally, North America drove 75% of GMV at $21.5 billion, up 24%, with same-day delivery at 42% in key cities. APAC hit 35% YoY growth to $4.3 billion, led by hyperlocal efforts in India and Southeast Asia. EMEA grew 12% to $2.9 billion. These results affirm our $500 million capex in AI, supply chain, and international expansion, and we're raising FY24 GMV guidance to $105-108 billion.

Turning to international market expansion, which is a cornerstone of our strategy as we scale into the $5.5 trillion global e-commerce opportunity. International markets now represent 28% of total GMV at $2.8 billion, up from 18% a year ago and growing 162% YoY, outpacing domestic growth. Orders surged 145% to 45 million units, with AOV steady at $62—5% above domestic—thanks to premium beauty and electronics. MAUs reached 32 million, up 130%, with 68% mobile penetration. Conversions improved to 4.2%, CAC fell 24% to $18, and 12-month LTV hit $285, up 35%, driven by a 42% subscription attach rate. Contribution margins expanded to 14.5%, up 320 basis points QoQ.

In Europe, 42% of international GMV at $1.18 billion, up 138%, UK GMV grew 155% to $520 million via Royal Mail partnerships for 92% on-time delivery, Germany orders up 210% post-DACH launch with Klarna BNPL uplift. France and Spain added $280 million, mitigating EU Digital Markets Act costs with GDPR tools; Italy influencer campaigns yielded 3x ROI.

Asia-Pacific, 35% at $980 million, up 195%, India led at $410 million with vernacular app and UPI boosting conversions 22%, Tier-2/3 cities via Delhivery at 48-hour delivery. Southeast Asia $420 million, Indonesia up 220% with Shopee and 55% repeat rates; China stabilized at $150 million via WeChat Mini Program.

Latin America, 15% at $420 million, up 120%, Brazil $250 million with Mercado Libre APIs and Pix; Mexico $110 million despite FX, Colombia growing with new micro-fulfillment.

Other regions added $220 million, UAE $80 million via Noon, Australia $80 million.

Our Global Gateway tech stack on Shopify Plus and BigCommerce enables 48-hour launches, with $150 million invested in AI personalization for 35% higher CTRs, multi-carrier logistics for 18% savings and 95% OTIF, 120+ payment gateways cutting abandonment to 22%, and blockchain for counterfeit reduction.

We're prioritizing high-velocity markets with 70% of $400 million capex on APAC/LatAm, guiding international GMV to $12-13 billion FY24 at 35% of total, EBITDA margins to 16%, with five new launches and $1 billion private label.

Next, seller performance metrics. We ended Q3 with 1.28 million active sellers—those with at least $1,000 trailing 12-month GMV—up 28% YoY and 8% QoQ. Annualized revenue per seller hit $52,400, up 18% YoY, from higher 12.8% take rates and service penetration. SMBs at 1.12 million (88%) grew 30%, averaging $28,000 ARPS with AI listing tools; enterprises at 162,000 contributed 45% revenue at $285,000 ARPS via FBS.

North America 795,000 actives, ARPS $61,200; Europe 282,000 up 35%, $48,700; APAC 154,000 up 45%, $39,800 with seller financing; LatAm 38,000 up 50%, $22,500.

GenAI Seller Suite automates pricing and forecasting for 15% GMV uplift, ad revenue up 22%, FBS throughput 40% higher. Top 10% sellers drive 65% volume. Guiding 1.5 million actives and $58-60,000 ARPS FY24.

On customer acquisition costs, our blended CAC was $38.42, down 16% YoY and 7% QoQ from $41.31, below industry $52. Payback compressed to 4.8 months, LTV/CAC at 4.2x from high-LTV categories with 45% repeat rates.

Paid search/shopping CAC $29.50, ROAS 8.2x via Performance Max and CDP; social $45.20, 5.9x ROAS with TikTok at sub-$35; affiliates $32.10, 6.8x; organic 28% of acquisitions. Marketing 11.2% of revenue.

ML bid optimization cut waste 24%, incrementality 68%, personalization 3x add-to-cart. North America $35.80 CAC, Europe $48.20, APAC/LatAm $62.40 but fast payback. Expect Q4 $37-39.

For net income and EPS, we beat with $285 million net income, up 32% YoY vs. $240 million guidance and $252 million consensus; diluted EPS $1.12, up 28% from $0.87, beating $0.92. Non-GAAP EPS $1.18 post-$15 million restructuring.

GMV $28.7 billion up 22%, revenue $6.8 billion up 25% at 11.2% take rates. Gross margin 43.2% up 210bps from RPA in 60% centers, fulfillment 18.2% down 180bps. EBITDA $562 million at 14.8% margin.

North America 52% GMV up 45%, APAC 38%, Europe 12%, LatAm 22%. Tailwinds: grocery 26%, AR try-on share gains, cost controls. Raising FY24 EPS midpoint 25%+. Balance sheet strong with $1.2 billion FCF, $400 million buybacks.

Finally, logistics and shipping costs rose to 14.2% of GMV from 11.8%, a $187 million headwind from Red Sea reroutes adding $4,200 per FEU and 12-18 days, ocean rates up 85%, last-mile $3.47 up 18% from port congestion and surcharges. APAC typhoons tripled air freight, EMEA CBAM and strikes.

Mitigations: AI routing saved 8%, WMS 24% efficiency, micro-fulfillment and drones. Nearshoring to 27% Mexico, safety stock up 15%, EV fleet 11% last-mile. Q4 13.8-14.2%, FY24 13.5%.

Now I'll turn it over to David Chen to discuss operations.

David Chen:
Thanks, Maria. Operationally, we focused on fulfillment optimization and supply chain diversification amid disruptions. Our shipping times improved by 15% to average 2.1 days domestically, with 97% on-time rates. Fulfillment costs declined 12% per unit to $3.20, despite headwinds, through robotics and regional hubs. We are implementing advanced warehouse management systems and drone pilots for same-day in key metros, targeting 20% volume coverage by year-end.

Now I'll turn it over to Emily Rivera.

Emily Rivera:
Thanks, David. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our TikTok Shop integrations and Performance Max campaigns, driving viral growth in Gen Z segments. Customer acquisition costs held at $38 efficiently, with ROAS exceeding 6x blended. Our brand awareness increased by 25% per Nielsen data. We are focusing on retention-first tactics like SMS personalization and omnichannel experiments to lift LTV 30%.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj Patel.

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Emily. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI/ML personalization and global logistics orchestration. Our website uptime was 99.95%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%, with 68% penetration internationally. We're investing in GenAI seller tools and recommendation engines, delivering 35% CTR uplift and supporting our international launches.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for Q&A: Press star one to queue. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On GMV, can you expand on the category drivers and how sustainable the beat is into Q4 holidays?

Alex Thompson:
Thanks, John. The category mix, especially fashion/beauty with our stylist tool and electronics flash sales, was key to the 22% YoY and beat. Sustainability comes from our 65 million active buyers and AI driving 35% of orders now. Q4 guidance of 25-28% YoY factors holiday spend projections and our supply chain readiness.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Maria, on net income and EPS, what drove the margin outperformance, and any color on FY24 guide raise?

Maria Lopez:
Hi Lisa. Margin expansion to 43.2% came from 210bps gross improvement via RPA and fulfillment efficiencies, plus take rate leverage. The EPS raise to $4.65-4.85 reflects broad-based strength, resilient demand in groceries, and cost controls saving $45 million QoQ. We're ahead on Flywheel 2.0 investments.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan.

Mike Patel:
David, logistics costs ticked up—how are disruptions impacting OTIF, and what's the path to 12-13% target?

David Chen:
Good question, Mike. Disruptions like Red Sea added costs, but OTIF held at 97% via AI routing and nearshoring. We're on track to 13.5% FY24 through micro-fulfillment scaling and EV fleets, with Q4 normalization expected.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Rodriguez with Barclays.

Anna Rodriguez:
Emily, impressive CAC compression—how are you balancing spend for international growth, and ROAS outlook?

Emily Rivera:
Thanks, Anna. Compression to $38 reflects ML optimization and 68% incrementality, with TikTok shining at 5.9x ROAS. For international, we're localizing like Klarna in Europe, expecting 10-12% YoY CAC reduction while scaling high-LTV cohorts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Citi.

Tom Lee:
Raj, seller metrics look strong—tech enablers for 1.28 million actives and ARPS growth, plus international tech stack?

Raj Patel:
Absolutely, Tom. GenAI Suite drove 15% GMV per listing uplift and 40% new seller adoption, boosting ARPS 18%. Global Gateway with TensorFlow personalization and multi-carrier APIs supports 95% OTIF internationally, positioning us for 1.5 million sellers.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Thompson for closing remarks.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Logistics and shipping costs: Impact of supply chain disruptions.
